δαγύς.definition: wax doll, used in magic rites, puppet, Theoc.2.110

δαίς.definition: personified, S.Fr.605. Rare in Prose as Hdt.1.133,211

δαίτης.definition: priest who divided the victims, E.Fr.472.12

δαιτρός.definition: one that carves and portions out; hereditary priest who officiated at the Dipolia, Porph.Abst.2.30

δάκος.definition: animal of which the bite; bite, sting, Pi.P.2.53, cf. Opp.H.2.454, 5.30

δάκρυ.definition: used by Poets metri gr. for in sg; generally, drop, Pi. l.c.; E.Med.1200

δαλός.definition: a kind of meteor, Arist.Mete.341b28; burnt-out torch: metaph. of an old man, AP12.41

δάρατος.definition: a Thessalian kind of bread, Maced; unleavened bread, Nic.Fr.184:—also fem. pl. cakes offered at marriage and registration ceremonies by a Michel995A5, al

δάρσις.definition: separation of parts united by cellular tissue by tearing, Herophil. ap. Gal.2.349, cf. Gal.2.483, etc

δάφνη.definition: sweet bay, Laurus nobilis, Od.9.183; Ruscus Hypoglossum, Thphr.HP1.10.8,3.17.4, Dsc.4.145

δειμός.definition: personified as accompanying etc., Il.4.44c, 1.37, 15.119, Hes.Th.934

δεῖνα.definition: in Com. as an interjection to express an idea which suddenly strikes one, by the way, mark you, Ar.V.524, Pax268, etc.: in later Prose, Luc.Vit.Auct.19

δεῖνος.definition: = a name for different round; a dance, Apolloph.1

δεκάς.definition: the company of Lycus, a name given to bribed dicasts at Athens, because the bribers were to be found near the statue of Lycus in the law- courts, Eratosth. ap. Harp.s.v

δέλτα.definition: indecl., the letter gen; anything shaped like a esp. island formed by the mouths of a large river, as the Nile, Hdt.2.13, etc.; of the Indus, Str.15.1.33, Arr.An.5.4.1, etc

δελφινίς.definition: prob. with dolphins for a base, Luc.Lex.7

δέμα.definition: band, Plb.6.33.11; =; Archit., clamp, dowel, IG7.3073.70

δεξιά.definition: Ion. , right hand; in welcoming or saluting , Ar.Nu.81; etc. ; esp. as a sign of assurance, pledge or treaty, . . Il.2.341; having exchanged assurances, X.An.7.3.1, cf. 1.1.6; bring pledges that he would not . ., ib.2…

δεξιότης.definition: dexterity, esp. of mind, sharpness; courtesy, kindliness , Ph.2.30

δερκευνής.definition: sleeping with the eyes open, Nic.Al.67

δέρτρον.definition: = caul or membrane which; in Od. l.c., is expld. by Gramm., as EM257.31, etc., of the vulture's beak: hence, of a sharp point, Lyc.880

δέσις.definition: binding together, Pl.Cra.418e; complication of a dramatic plot, opp. Arist.Po.1455b26

δεσμός.definition: ligature, Arist.HA495b13, al; in Hp.Fract.37 is expld. by Gal. ad loc. as ankylosis

δέτις.definition: torch, Hp. ap. Erot; head of garlic , Id.l.c

δεῦμα.definition: that which is steeped, seethed, boiled flesh, dub. in Pi.O.1.50; cf

δεύτερος.definition: second, (perh. from with Comp; next in Order , in Il. of one who comes in second in a race, 23.265; 22.207; . . . . next, 20.273, etc.; no second grief, i.e. none hereafter like this, 23.46; as Comp., c. gen., after m…

δεχάς.definition: receptacle, coined by Pythag. to expl. Ph.2.184, Theol.Ar.59, Ascl.in Metaph.38.31, etc

δηϊοτής.definition: battle-strife, the battle, Il.3.20, etc.; mortal struggle, death, Od.12.257; cf

δηϊφόβος.definition: Dor. scaring the foe, dub. in Alc.28:—in Hom. only pr. n

δῆμος.definition: Dor. , district, country; the people, inhabitants of such a district, Il.3.50, cf. h.Cer.271; A.Pers.732

δημός.definition: fat, . . Il.23.750, cf. Hes.Th.538, Ar.V.40, etc.; with fat above and fat below, Il.23.243; of men, 8.380

διάδεξις.definition: passage, Hp.Epid.6.2.14; transition from one disease to another, ib.1.1

διάζωμα.definition: that which is put round as a girdle; a girdle, drawers, Th.1.6

διαθήκη.definition: disposition of property by; mystic deposits on which the common weal depended, prob. oracles , Din.1.9 codd

διαθιγή.definition: mutual contact, Leucipp. and Democr. ap. Arist.Metaph.985b15, al.; v.l. perh. =

διάκαμψις.definition: bending, of the body, in exercise, Archig. ap. Aët.12.1

διακήρυξις.definition: sale by auction, and Adj. pertaining to such a sale, Gloss

διακοπή.definition: gash, cleft, as in the skull, Hp.VC7; rupture of a blood-vessel, Gal.19.457

δίακτος.definition: carried through pipes, of oils or unguents used at the bath, CIG2820 , 3871b ; IGRom.4.860

διάνημα.definition: that which is spun, a thread, Pl.Plt.309b

διαπασῶν.definition: i.e. concord of the first and last notes, octave; more correctly divisim, Pl.R.432a; Plu.2.1019b

διάπεζος.definition: of women's robes, either reaching to the feet or having a border , Callix.2

διάπηξις.definition: fastening together, structure, bodily frame, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

διάπλοος.definition: Adj., sailing across or sailing continually, they kept them at the oar, A.Pers.382

διαρροή.definition: channel, pipe, the wind-; flowing through, ebb and flow, D.C.39.41

διαρρωγή.definition: gap, interstice, left in applying a bandage, Hp.Art.35

διαρρώξ.definition: as Subst., rent, of the Straits of Messina, ib.5.216

διάστρα.definition: warp set up in a loom, Gloss

διάστρωμα.definition: abstract of title-deeds in land; = digestum, Gloss

διασφάξ.definition: any opening made by; Medic., of divisions of blood-vessels, Hp.Loc.hom.3; fissure in the liver, Herophil. ap. Gal.2.570

διατομή.definition: cutting through, severance, A.Th.934 (lyr; sharp edge, ib.1.31

διάτονος.definition: on the stretch, vehement; extending from front to back, of bonding courses in a wall, Vitr.2.8.7

διάτριμμα.definition: a sore from the skin being rubbed off in riding, Gloss

διαφυή.definition: natural break, joint, suture; stratum or vein of earth, stone, metal, Thphr.Lap.63; D.S.3.12

διάχυτον.definition: wine made from partly dried grapes, Plin.HN14.84

διάψαλμα.definition: musical interlude, used by the LXX, in the Psalms, for the Hebr. Selah

διεδρεία.definition: sitting apart, of birds whose position was ominous of strife, opp. Arist.HA608b27 , Id.EE1236b10

διέλασις.definition: driving through, of a nail; charge or exercise of cavalry, X.Eq.Mag.3.4

δίζωος.definition: with two lives, i. e. Sisyphus, who returned from Hades, Dosiad.Ara17

δίϊξις.definition: interpenetration, Procl.in Ti.2.88 D., cf. Olymp.in Alc.p.215 C.; penetration of sensations to consciousness, Prisc.Lyd.14.22

διΐφιλος.definition: dear to Zeus, usu. written divisim, Il.1.74, etc., but cf. EM275.6, etc

δικαία.definition: Ion. poet. for like for Cerc.18.5, cf. EM24.48

δίκαιος.definition: also E.Heracl.901; observant of duty to gods and men, righteous, Od.13.209, etc.; Hp.Medic.2; Hdt.1.96; opp. A.Th.598, cf. 610; Pl.Grg.507b; S.Ant.791 ; also of actions, etc., righteous, a thing rightly said, Od.18.41…

δίκη.definition: custom, usage, this; adverb. in acc. in the way of, after the manner of, c. gen., Pi.P.2.84; S.Fr.659; Pl.Lg.705e; in later Prose, Arist.Mu.395b22, Luc.Dem.Enc.31, Alciphr.1.6, etc.: mostly of living creatures or pers…

δίκηλος.definition: with double hernia, Heliod; with double hydrocele, Paul.Aeg.6.62

δίνουμμον.definition: coin of the value of two , Gloss

δίξυλος.definition: with two blocks, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.8.9

δίοδος.definition: way through, passage, pass, of Thermopylae; passing through the bowels, Hp.Prorrh.1.127

δίοζος.definition: with two knots or eyes, Thphr.HP1.8.3

διολκή.definition: diversity of opinion, S.E.M.8.322, Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.5

δίολκος.definition: slipway for passage of ships across the Isthmus of Corinth, Str.7.2.1

διόνυξ.definition: double nail, as a superficial measure, HeroStereom.1.95

δίοψις.definition: a view through, Plu.2.915a; metaph., consideration, Pl.Ti.40d codd

δίπαις.definition: with two children; a dirge chanted by one's two children, A.Ch.334

διπλόθριξ.definition: gen. with geminate leaves, of the stone-pine, Dionys.Av.1.27

διπλόος.definition: contr. Ion. fem; by mutual slaughter, S.Ant.14

δίσκος.definition: anything quoit-shaped; dish, trencher, AP11.371 , Lib.Decl.30.24; salver, BGU388ii22

δίστροφος.definition: doubly twisted, of cords, Meges ap; of two turns, Papp.1110.15

δίυγρος.definition: washed out, pale, Hp.Int.43; of a melting glance, AP12.68.7

δίφας.definition: a kind of serpent, Artem.2.13; cf

δίχωρον.definition: a measure of wine in Egypt, = eight BGU531 ii 5 , etc

δίψα.definition: c. gen., thirst for, Pl.R.437d: metaph., Pi.P.9.104.—The form occurs in Opp.C.4.339, and in codd. of A.Ch.756; cf

διωρία.definition: either fixed space or interval, or appointed time, J.BJ5.9.1

διωχής.definition: that will hold two, Pherecr.3, Paus.Gr.Fr.132

δόκημα.definition: vision, fancy, E.HF111; opinion, expectation, Id.HF771

δοκίς.definition: plank, Hp.Fract.13, X.Cyn.9.15; screen or shield used by sappers, = Ph.Bel.81.28, al

δοκοθήκη.definition: stone with hole for insertion of roof- beam, IG11.161 A 55

δόλιχος.definition: the long course, in racing, opp; a measure of length, = 12 stades, HeroGeom.4.13

δόλος.definition: prop. bait for fish, Od.12.252: hence; generally, any trick or stratagem, Il.6.187, etc.: in pl., wiles, 3.202; 4.339, etc

δόλωμα.definition: trick, deceit, A.Ch.1003; stratagem, ruse, Aen. Tact.8.2

δόμος.definition: house, Il.2.513, Sapph.1.7, etc.; also, part of a house, room, chamber, Od.8.57, 22.204: freq. in pl. for a house, Hes.Op.96, etc.; freq. in Trag., A.Supp.433, etc.: chiefly poet., or being used in Prose

δόναξ.definition: bed of reeds, App.BC3.67, al; anything made of reed

δόξα.definition: after Hom., notion, opinion, judgement, whether well grounded or not, Parm.1.30, cf. 8.51; A.Pers.28 ; S.Fr.235; Id.Tr.718; with or without Pl.Grg.472e, Phlb.41b: opp. Id.Tht.187b sq., R.506c, Hp.Lex4, Arist.Metaph.10…

δορά.definition: skin when taken off, hide, of; rarely, skin on the living body, Ph.2.100, Hld.9.18

δόρπιος.definition: belonging to the feast; Subst. supper-time, v.l. in Hp.Epid.5.22

δόρυ.definition: Att. gen. rare in Poets, as; of a ship, Pi.P.4.27, E.Cyc.15; S.Ph.721 ; also alone, A.Pers.411, Ag.1618, E.Hel.1611; Id.Andr.793; also of oars, Hymn.Is.152

δορυξεῖον.definition: workshop where spear-shafts are made, Id

δουκηνάριος.definition: = Lat. ducenarius, official receiving; fem. assessment of 200,000 sesterces, ib.1274.14

δοῦρας.definition: a nom. sg. formed from the Homeric pl. , AP6.97

δραϝεός.definition: uncertain object dedicated to Athena, GDI1537

δράμις.definition: a kind of loaf, Maced. word, Seleuc. ap. Ath.3.114b

δράξ.definition: handful, Batr.237; the hand, LXXIs.40.12 ; Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44; the claw of the constellation Leo, Ptol.Alm.7.5

δρῖλος.definition: expld. by Lat. verpus, sens. obsc., AP11.197 ; Supp.Epigr.2.353

δρόμος.definition: course, race, in Il.mostly of; foot-race, as a contest, IG2.594.11, al.: prov., to run for one's life, Hdt.8.74; Ar.V.375; Pl.Tht.173a: generally, contest, i. e. a pugilistic contest, Pi.I.5.60

δυοειδής.definition: of two forms, double, dual, Porph.VP50; Herm.in Phdr.p.167 A. Adv. Dam.Pr.55

δύστηνος.definition: Dor. wretched, unhappy; mostly of persons, as always in Hom. and mostly Trag., A.Pers.909 , etc.; unhappy are they whose sons . . , Il.6.127

δύστομος.definition: hard-mouthed, of a horse; hard to pronounce, Phld.Po.2.15

δύσχορτος.definition: with little grass or food, inhospitable dwellings, E.IT219

δυωδεκάς.definition: the number twelve, Procl.in; twelfth part, of the signs of the zodiac, Arat.555 , 703; of an hour, AP9.779, 782

δῶ.definition: shortd. Ep. form for house, dwelling, Hom. only in nom. as Od.1.392, and acc. as Il.1.426.—As pl. for only in Hes.Th.933

δωρίτης.definition: game in which the conqueror received a present, Plu.2.820d

δῶρον.definition: gift, present, gift of honour; presents, as retaining fees or bribes, D.18.109, Jusj.ib.24.150, Arist.Ath.55.5, SIG953.7 , etc. : hence in Att. law, an indictment for being bribed, Aeschin.3.232, etc., cf. Harp.; to b…

δωτήρ.definition: giver, givers of good, i.e. the gods, Od.8.325, Hes.Th.46, etc.: voc. Rev.Arch.1911.439

δᾳδίον.definition: Dim. of splinter of pine wood; dilator , Hp.Mul.1.13,2.133

δᾳδόομαι.definition: Pass., become afflicted with resin- glut, Thphr.CP5.11.3

δᾳδουργός.definition: one who cuts pines for torches, ib.3.9.3

δᾳδουχέω.definition: carry a torch, esp. in pageants, E.Tr.343; hold the office of 1.1, IG2.1413,1414

δαιδάλλω.definition: Act. only in pres. and impf.:—work cunningly; metaph., Pi.O.5.21; Id.Parth.2.32:—Pass., Id.O.1.29; ib.2.53; Id.N.11.18

δαίδαλος.definition: cunningly or curiously wrought; spotted, speckled, or perh. rather, sheeny, shot with light, of fish, Opp.C.1.58

δαιμονίς.definition: fem. of Procl.in Ti.1.47 D., in Prm.p.643S., Herm.in Phdr.p.87 A.:—also PMag.Leid.W.16.48

δαίνυμι.definition: c. acc. pers., feast one on a thing, . . Hdt.1.162, cf. E.Or.15; thou shalt be my living feast, A.Eu.305

δαιτρεία.definition: place where meat is cut up, Hdn.Epim.19

δαιτρεύω.definition: divide, esp. cut up meat, to cut up and roast it, Od.15.323; . . to carve, 14.433; to cut up for distribution among the people, Il.11.705, cf. 688; of the Amazons, A.R.2.1176; Them.Or.13.171c; of animals, devour prey,…

δακνάζω.definition: metaph. in Pass., to be afflicted, mournful, imper. A.Pers.571

δάκνω.definition: Hippon.49.6 , A.Th.399, etc.: fut; metaph. of pungent smoke and dust, sting, Ar.Ach.18, Lys.298, Pl.822; of dry winds, Hp.Aph.3.17

δάκρυμα.definition: that which is wept for, a subject

δακρυπλώω.definition: swim with tears, of drunken men, Od.19.122

δακρύω.definition: intr., weep, shed tears, Od. l.c., etc.: c. acc. cogn., to lament with tears, S.Aj.580: c. gen. causae, E.HF528 ; to flood them with tears, Id.Hel.948; X.HG7.2.9; Isoc.4.168:— Pass., pf. to be in tears, Il.16.7; 22.49…

δαμνάω.definition: = Hom. only in 3sg. pres. Od.11.221: impf. Il.21.52, Sapph.Supp.1.12; Il.16.103, al.; Ion. h.Ven.251: 2sg. pres. Thgn.1388 ; imper. Sapph.1.3

δάμνημι.definition: = . . Il.5.893; ib.746, etc.; Thgn.173; . . Alc.92:—Med., Il.14.199; Od.14.488; Hes.Th.122, cf. Archil.85, A.Pr.165, Q.S.11.25:—Pass., Il.11.309; 8.244; 13.16; A.Supp.904 ; imper. Maiist.51: pf. part. forced, seduced,…

δάπτω.definition: fut. Il.13.831: aor. poet. Pi.N.8.23, Opp.H.3.333:—devour, as wild beasts, Il.16.159, etc.; Emp.136; of fire, Il.23.183; of a spear, rend, 13.831, cf. A.Pr.370; of moths and worms, Pi.Fr.222; tear with the nails, A.Su…

δασύπους.definition: rough-foot, i.e. hare, Lepus; in Plin., Prob. rabbit, Lepus cuniculus, HN8.219, 10.173

δατέομαι.definition: Il.18.264, etc., irreg. inf. (v.l; measured the ground with their feet, Il.23.121

δατητής.definition: in Att. law, liquidator of estates or partnerships, Arist.Ath.56.6, etc

δαψιλής.definition: abundant, plentiful, Hp.Acut.65; of space, ample, wide, Lyc.957

δειδίσσομαι.definition: later Att. impf; intr., fear, . . Hp.Mul.1.25; . . A.R.2.1219, cf. Plu.Dio57: c. acc., to be afraid of, Orph.A.56, etc.: aor. App.BC5.79; Aret.CA1.1; Luc.Sol.5

δείδω.definition: 1st sg. pf. in pres. sense; abs., Hom., etc

δειελιάω.definition: take an afternoon meal, Od.17.599, cf. Ath.5.193a

δεικανάω.definition: point out, show, in Ion. and Ep

δείκνυμι.definition: show, point out, Il.3.452; . . S.Ph.609, cf. 492,630; experiment will show, Cratin.177, cf. Pl.Tht.200e, Hp.Ma.288b; alone, time will show, Ar.Ra.1261; point towards, Hdt.4.150:—Med., h.Merc.367

δεικτήριον.definition: place for showing; at Samos, place

δείλομαι.definition: verge towards afternoon, the sun was westering, Od.7.289; Delph. and Locr., =

δειπνέω.definition: c. acc., make a meal on bread, Hes.Op.442; Ephipp.15.13; Alex.221.17; Mnesim.7; of parasites, freq. in Com., Theopomp.34, Eub.72, etc.; also Ar.Pl.890

δειπνίζω.definition: Att. fut. Diph.62: aor. X.Cyr.4.5.5 :—entertain at dinner, Od.4.535; Hdt.7.118; IG5.1346: also c. acc. cogn., give one a dinner, MatroConv.2:—Pass., the applause of spectators bribed by dinners, Plu.2.92e

δειρόπαις.definition: producing young by the neck, as weasels were supposed to do, Lyc.843

δειροτομέω.definition: fut. cut the throat of a person, Il.21.89, cf. 555, Od.22.349

δεκάδραχμος.definition: at the price of ten drachmae; Subst. taxpayer assessed at ten ib.118ii9

δεκάμαζος.definition: with ten breasts, of Ephesian Artemis, Epigr.Gr.406.10

δεκάμυξος.definition: with ten wicks, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens235

δεκάσχημος.definition: with ten forms, of certain verses, Ps.-Plu.Metr. p.471 B

δεκατεύω.definition: exact tithe from, D.22.77; in war, take out the tenth man for execution, decimate, D.C.48.42, etc

δεκατόω.definition: take tithe of a person, Ep.Hebr.7.6:—Pass., pay tithe, ib.9

δεκέτης.definition: lasting ten years, S.Ph.715; ten years old, fem. Ar.Lys.644

δέκτωρ.definition: one who takes upon himself or on his own head, A.Eu.204

δελεάζω.definition: entice or catch by a bait; c. acc. cogn., put it on the hook as a bait, Hdt.2.70; but bait it with a fig, Luc.Pisc.47; to catch others. ib.48

δέμω.definition: rare in pres. and impf., Ep. impf; generally, construct, prepare, h.Merc.87; Lat. munire viam, Hdt.2.124:— Pass., Id.7.200: metaph. of persons, Haussoullier Miletp.141

δενδίλλω.definition: turn the eyes or glance quickly, . . Il.9.180; A.R.3.281.—Ep. word, also S.Fr.1039

δενδρόω.definition: turn into a tree, Nonn.D.43.234:—Med; Pass., grow into a tree, Thphr.HP1.9.4

δέρκομαι.definition: Il.11.37, etc.: impf; look with favour on, of Destiny, Pi.P.3.85

δέρω.definition: Ar.V.485, Pl.Euthd.285c, etc.:-also Hdt.2.39, Ar.Nu.442, Av.365, Cratin.361: impf. Il.23.167, Ep. Od.8.61: fut. Ar.Eq.370: aor. Il.2.422, Hdt.5.25, Pl.R.616a:-Med., v. fut. Ev.Marc.13.9, POxy.653b : aor. Men.Mon.422, …

δευτερόω.definition: do the second time: repeat; change, ib.Je.2.36

δεύω.definition: mix a dry mass with liquid, so as to make it fit to knead, Ar.Fr.271; X.Oec.10.11; Id.Cyr.6.2.28; knead up with meal, D.H.7.72

δέφω.definition: soften by working with the hand: sens. obsc., = Lat. masturbari, Eub.120.5:—Med., Ar.Eq.24, Pax290

δέχομαι.definition: Ion., Aeol., Cret. Hdt.9.91; of things as the object, take, accept, receive, etc., 1.20, etc.; Pl.R.416e; Th.1.90; Od.19.355; Pl.Grg.499c; Plb.33.6.2, etc.; receive something at the hand of another, Il.2.186, cf. IG12…

δέψω.definition: aor. work or knead a thing till it is soft, Od.12.48; Hdt.4.64

δέω.definition: imper. 3pl. Od.12.54 codd. (v; alone, bind, keep in bonds, says Hephaistos, pointing to the nets in which he had caught Ares, Od.8.352; A.Eu.641; Th.1.30; Lex ap.D.24.105, etc

δηθύνω.definition: pres. and impf. only, Ep. subj. Od.12.121: :—tarry, delay, Il.6.503, AP5.222.6 ; of disease, to be prolonged, Aret.SD1.2; to be slow of hearing, Orph.L.467

δηϊόω.definition: Ep.opt. Od.4.226, part; rend, tear, cleave, . . were cleaving shields, Il.5.452, etc.; of a spear, cut asunder, 14.518; of savage beasts, 17.65, cf. 16.158; having had his beard cut off, Luc.DMort.10.11

δηλέομαι.definition: Dor. Theoc.15.48: fut; mostly of persons, hurt, do a mischief to, by accident, Il.23.428; also on purpose, 4.67; . . did thee a mischief, i.e. slew thee, Od.11.401; . . 22.368; of the sword, ib.278; h.Merc.541; Mimn.7…

δήλησις.definition: mischief, Hdt.1.41, cf. 4.112; Thphr.HP7.13.4; injury of health, Hp.Jusj

δήλωμα.definition: a means of making known, Pl.Lg.792a, Plu.2.78e, etc.: pl., ib.62d

δήλωσις.definition: pointing out, explanation, Th.1.73; direction, order, Pl.Lg.942c

διοϊστεύω.definition: shoot an arrow between; abs., thou mightest reach it with an arrow, i. e. thou art but a bow-shot from it, 12.102

διοκνέω.definition: to be much afraid, Antig.Car. ap. Ath.13.607e

διόλλυμι.definition: blot out of one's mind, forget, ib.318

διοπτεύω.definition: watch accurately, spy about; take a sight, HeroBel.86.7; esp. through the Id.Dioptr.4

διοπτήρ.definition: spy, scout, Il.10.562: in; the optiones and tesserarii of the Romans, Plu.Galb.24

διόπτρα.definition: optical instrument for measuring angles; aperture-sight in a torsion-engine, Ph.Bel.64.9, 76.48

διοργανίζω.definition: dispose suitably, in Pass., Zos.Alch.p.251 B., Syn. Alch.p.62 B

διορθεύω.definition: = sq., only in E.Supp.417 not judging rightly of words

διορθόω.definition: make straight, Hp.Art.38; tell my tale aright, Pi.O.7.21

διόρυγμα.definition: cut, canal, as that across the; digging through, house-breaking, LXXEx.22.2, Je.2.34

διουρέω.definition: pass in urine, Dsc.Eup.2.65:—Pass; intr., pass urine, Id.Aër.9

δίπαλτος.definition: brandished with both hands, E.IT323; lightning hurled by Zeus with both hands, i. e. with all his might, Id.Tr.1103 ; . . all the host would kill me with sword brandished in both hands, i. e. with all their might, S.A…

διπλόω.definition: repeat a process, Arist.APo.91a21; double; repay twofold, Apoc.18.6

δίπλωσις.definition: compounding of words; doubling, Gal.UP9.6 ; esp. in Alch., Zos.Alch.p.183 B., cf. PHolm.2.18, al

δίπολις.definition: of or divided into two cities, Str.3.4.8, 14.2.15

δίπορος.definition: with two roads or openings, E.Tr.1097

δίπους.definition: jerboa, which springs from its two hind feet, Hdt.4.192; two feet long, Pl.Men.83d; Id.Plt.266b

δίπρῳρος.definition: a ship double- prowed and double-sterned, i. e. a twin ship, Callix.1, Promathidas ap.Ath.11.489b

δίπτερος.definition: two-winged, of insects, opp; temple with double peristyle, Vitr.3.2.7

δίπτωτος.definition: having one form for two cases, A.D.Pron.91.7

δίπυρος.definition: twice fired, i. e. baked, =; Hecate holding up two flaming torches, Ar.Ra.1361

δίρρυμος.definition: with two poles, i. e. three horses, Id.Pers.47

δισιτέομαι.definition: eat two meals a day, Herod.Med. ap. Aët.9.13

δισκέω.definition: pitch the quoit, . . . . Od.8.188; having made a long throw, Pi.I.2.35; IG5.828 :—Pass., to be hurled, of a person, E.Ion1268 ; of a squid, AP9.227

δίστολος.definition: in pairs, two together, or simply, two, S.OC1055

διτονέω.definition: have a double accent, A.D.Synt.307.15; or two accents, Id.Pron.60.16

διυλίζω.definition: strain, filter thoroughly, Mim; strain off, Ev.Matt.23.24

διυπνίζω.definition: awake from sleep, trans., Ael.NA7.46; fall asleep, Simp.in Ph.1258.25

διφάω.definition: only pres., search after, . . Il.16.747; Hes.Op.374; Call.Epigr.33, cf. Fr.165; search them well, Thphr.Char.10.6: abs., Herod.6.73; . . Nonn.D.48.592:—Ion. AP9.559

δίφορος.definition: bearing fruit twice in the year; bearing two kinds of fruit, Ph.2.369

δίφραξ.definition: poet. for seat, chair, Theoc.14.41:—also Hom.Epigr.15.8

δίφριος.definition: of a chariot: neut. pl. as Adv., dragged at the chariot wheels, AP7.152

διφρυγής.definition: twice roasted: baked clay or pyrites from copper-mines, Dsc.5.103, 125, Gal.12.214

διχάζω.definition: fut. Plot.5.3.10:—divide in two; divide by two, Nicom.Ar.1.7, al

διχάλα.definition: Dor. for the fork of the legs, Medici ap.Gal.14.707

διχασμός.definition: division into two parts, Aq.De.14.6; division by two, Nicom.Ar.1.10

διχοστατέω.definition: stand apart, disagree; feel doubts, Alex.Aphr.Pr.Praef

διχοτομέω.definition: cut in twain: bisect a line; punish with the last severity, Ev.Matt.24.51

διχοτομία.definition: dividing in two, of the moon's; point of bisection, Archim.Aequil.1.6, al

διχοφυΐα.definition: a disease of the hair, when it splits, Id.19.430

διχρονία.definition: in Metric, two short syllables; Pythag. name for six, Theol.Ar.37

δίψακος.definition: prob. a kind of diabetes, attended with; teasel, Dipsacus fullonum, Dsc.3.11, Gal.11.864

δίψιος.definition: causing thirst, Hermipp. ap. J.Ap.1.22; Nic.Th.147; cf. II

δίω.definition: Ep. Verb , only pres. and impf. Med. :—put to flight, Il.12.276; Od.20.343; . . 21.370; . . . . Il.22.189; . . 16.246; rarely, drive, . . . . 15.681; also in A., pursuing a dishonoured office, Eu.385 ; and intr. folld…

δίωγμα.definition: pursuit, chase, A.Eu.139; that which is chased, X.Cyn.3.9

διωθέω.definition: aor. Hom. , X.HG2.1.8; thrust through, X.HG2.1.8, Plb.21.28.14

διωκτέος.definition: verb. Adj. of to be pursued; of objects, to be pursued, Pl.Tht.167d, etc

διώκω.definition: pursue, chase, in war or hunting, Il.22.199, etc.: abs., 5.223, cf. Hdt.9.11:—Med., chase one over or across . . , Il.21.602, Od.18.8

διωνυμία.definition: pair of names or double name, Vett.Val.187.25, Man.4.376, Hdn.Fig.p.103S

δίωσις.definition: pushing asunder, forcing open; putting off 'sine die', Id.Rh.1372a33

διωσμός.definition: = foreg. I, in gymnastics; in surgery, pushing through of embedded weapons, Paul.Aeg.6.88

διωστήρ.definition: instrument for pushing out embedded; pole running through rings, for carrying the ark, LXXEx.38.10

δνοπαλίζω.definition: shake violently, fling down, Il.4.472; 'wrap thy old cloak about thee', Od.14.512:—Pass., of the polypus, its arms wave about, Opp.H.2.295

δνόφος.definition: darkness, dusk, gloom, Simon.37.8: pl., A.Ch.52 .—Poet. word, though its collat. form occurs in later Prose

δοιάζω.definition: or consider in two ways, be in two minds: hence, have a mind to, aor., B.10.87; also was hesitating between.., A.R.3.819; . . when she imagined a noise, ib.955:— Med., she doubted, ib.770; imagined they saw, Id.4.576

δοιώ.definition: = , = indecl., Hom.; commonly masc., Il.3.236, al.; but neut. in 24.648

δοκεύω.definition: keep an eye upon, watch narrowly; expect, c. acc., Arat.987, al.: c. gen., Id.813

δοκέω.definition: Il.7.192, Att. impf. Ep; fut. and aor. 1 Pi.N.4.37, h.Merc.208, etc.: pf. inferred from plpf. D.C.44.26:—Pass., aor. Plb.21.10.8, etc., Antipho2.2.2: pf. Hdt.8.100, etc.: plpf. Id.9.74

δολιόω.definition: 3pl. impf. deal treacherously with one, LXXPs.5.10, al.: abs., to be treacherous, Sm.Pr.26.19

δολοφρονέων.definition: planning craft, wily-minded, Il.3.405, Od.10.339, Archil.93

δομή.definition: building, dub. l. in J.AJ15.11.3, cf; Alex. word for A.R.3.1395, Nic.Th.153, Lyc.334,597,783

δονακοδίφης.definition: poet. one who searches among reeds, prob. in ib.10.22

δονέω.definition: shake, of the effects of the wind; drive about, . . . . Od.22.300; disturb, terrify, Tim.Pers.222: hence of love, agitate, excite, Sapph.40, Ar.Ec.954 ; Pi.P.4.219, cf. 6.36 ; B.1.69 ; . . Mnesim.4.60; Alciphr.Fr.6.12…

δοξάζω.definition: think, imagine, c. acc. et inf., A.Ag.673; c. part., will suppose that he hears, A.Supp.60

δοξόω.definition: only Pass., have the character or credit of being, Hdt.8.124; Id.7.135, cf. 9.48

δορκαδίζω.definition: bound like an antelope, of the pulse, Herophil. ap. Gal.8.556, al

δορόω.definition: coat, plaster, IG22.463.68, cf. 2.1054.58, dub. in ib.11.287A121

δουπέω.definition: fut. AP9.427 : Ep. aor. Il.4.504, al.; also 11.45: pf. 23.679, Nic.Al.15, A.R.1.1304, Euph.40; not freq. exc. in Ep.: :—sound heavy or dead; in Hom., of the heavy thud of a corpse, opp. the clashing of the armour, Il.…

δοχεύς.definition: recipient, esp. of oracles or inspiration, Orac. ap. Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.9, Herm.in Phdr.pp.105,111 A

δραγμεύω.definition: collect the corn into sheaves, Il.18.555

δραγμίς.definition: small handful, pinch, v.l. for Hp.Morb.2.55

δρακοντίτης.definition: dragon-stone, conferring sharp vision, Ptol.Chenn.p.192 W

δρασκάζω.definition: attempt an escape, Lex ap.Lys.10.17: prov., of those who 'bury their head in the sand', Zen.3.74

δράσσομαι.definition: Att. Hdt.3.13; impf; lay hold of, E.Tr.750; having seized [them] by the throat, Theoc.24.28, cf. 25.145, POxy.1298.10 : metaph., D.S.12.67; , Call.Epigr.1.14; AP11.238 ; Theoc.30.9; sounds the mouth has to grip, i.e. …

δραχμή.definition: prop. as much as one can hold; a weight, drachm, prob.in IG12.10.4, Thphr.Od.17, etc

δράω.definition: Aeol. 3pl. Alc.Supp.27.11, subj; of things, Ar.Eq.237; Luc.Im.1: so, generally, to be active, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.135, cf. Prisc.Lyd.4.10

δρέπτω.definition: poet. for sq., pluck, Ep.impf. Mosch.2.69:—more freq. in Med., Opp.C.2.38, APl.4.231 , etc

δρομίας.definition: a kind of fish, Eratosth.Fr.12; horseman-crab, Ael.NA7.24

δροσία.definition: poet. foam of a horse's mouth, Orac. ap. Luc.Alex.53; dew, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.172

δρυΐνας.definition: serpent living in hollow oaks, Nic.Th.411, Dsc.Ther.11

δρύπτω.definition: metaph., Herod.8.2.—Poet., X. and later Prose, as Philostr.VA3.38

δυαδίζω.definition: make into a dyad, in Pass., Dam.Pr.147

δυάζω.definition: express in the dual number, Eust.47.28; Pass., to be impressed with the sense of a thing's being double, see double, etc., S.E.M.7.193

δυάς.definition: the number two, Pl.Phd.101c, Prm.149c; dyad, Arist.Metaph.1081a14, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.58.12

δυάω.definition: plunge in misery, . . Od.20.195:— Pass., pf. part. Hsch

δυειδής.definition: of the class of the dyad, Dam.Pr.189

δύναμαι.definition: to be able, strong enough to do, c. inf. pres. et aor., Il.19.163, 1.562, etc.: fut. inf. is f.l. in S.Ph.1394, Plb.21.11.13, etc.: freq. abs., with inf. supplied from the context, if at least thou canst , Il.1.393: a…

δυναστεύω.definition: hold power or lordship, be powerful or; Math., in Pass., to be concerned with powers of numbers, Pl.R.546b

δυσαγρέω.definition: have bad sport in fishing, Plu.Ant.29

δύσαυλος.definition: bad for lodging, inhospitable, of frost, S.Ant.356

δύσβατος.definition: hard to traverse, impassable; trodden in sorrow, A.Pers.1069

δυσγνωσία.definition: difficulty of knowing, I did not know thy face, E.El.767

δύσγονος.definition: conceiving with difficulty, Vett. Val.18.24, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.207

δυσδερκής.definition: ill to look upon, grim, ugly, ib.3.263; hard to see, faint, Id.C.1.102, cf. 451

δύσεδρος.definition: bringing evil in one's abode; fitting ill, awry, D.H.Comp.6

δυσεμέω.definition: not to vomit easily, Philum. ap. Aët.9.23

δύσερως.definition: madly or disastrously loving; laggard in love, Theoc.1.85, 6.7

δυσήλιος.definition: Dor. ill-sunned, sunless; too much sunned, parched, Trag.Adesp.340

δυσήνιος.definition: = foreg., refractory, Epict.Gnom.63; Men.803. B. = ill at ease, uneasy, codd

δυσθαλπής.definition: hard to warm: chilly; over-warm, burning hot, Q.S.11.156 codd

δυσιερέω.definition: to have bad omens in a sacrifice, Plu.Caes.63, 2.587c

δύσιππος.definition: hard to ride in: parts unfit for cavalry-service, X.HG3.4.12; Plu.Phil.14

δυσκαής.definition: hard to burn, burning badly, Plu.2.952c

δύσκηλος.definition: past remedy, A.Eu.825 : but perh. rather formed by analogy from hence, spiteful

δυσκληρέω.definition: to be unlucky in one's lot, esp. in standing for an office, opp. Pl.Lg.690c

δύσκλιτος.definition: hard to inflect, irregular, title of work by Eulogius, EM809.33

δύσκολπος.definition: with luckless womb, of a woman whose child was dead before birth, AP7.583

δύσκροτος.definition: badly put together: Adv. to be in bad condition, MenoIatr.13.20, cf. 9.16

δύσλοφος.definition: hard for the neck, hard to bear; impatient of the yoke, Ael.NA16.9. Adv. E.Tr.303

δυσμαχέω.definition: fight in vain against or fight an unholy fight with, S.Tr.492; Plu.2.371a: abs., fight desperately, ib.661c

δύσμαχος.definition: hard to fight with, unconquerable; generally, difficult, A.Ag.1561

δύσνιφος.definition: snowed upon, Nonn.D.2.685; chilly, wintry, ib.3.210; ib.13.533

δυσνόητος.definition: hard to be understood, Darius ap; Act., slow of understanding, Vett.Val.345.26

δυσνομία.definition: Ep. and Ion. lawlessness, bad constitution, Sol.4.32: personified in Hes.Th.230

δύσορμος.definition: with bad anchorage; Act., that detained the fleet in harbour or that kept it from reaching harbour, foul winds, A.Ag.193

δύσοσμος.definition: Ion. ill-smelling; bad for scent, in hunting, X.Cyn.5.3

δυσπαθής.definition: feeling to excess, opp; not easily affected, ib.651c: abs., impassive, ib.454c, Luc.Anach.24, Plot.1.4.8

δυσπενθής.definition: bringing sore affliction, direful; bitterly lamented, of the dead, Opp.H.4.261

δύσπνοος.definition: contr. scant of breath; unfit to breathe, Thphr.Ign.24

δύσρητος.definition: that should not be spoken; hard to give a name to, Gal.12.501

δυσροέω.definition: flow ill, i.e.to be unlucky, Arr.Epict.1.28.30, al

δύσροια.definition: bad circulation, Anon.Lond.4.17: metaph., ill luck, misfortune, Arr.Epict.2.17.18

δυστυχής.definition: unlucky, unfortunate, of persons and; of the Erinyes, ill-starred, harbingers of ill, A.Eu.791

δυσφημία.definition: ill language, esp. words of ill omen; blasphemy, slander, D.H.6.48, etc

δυσφορία.definition: malaise, discomfort, Hp.Acut.54; vexation, distress, Epicur.Fr.445 , Simp.in Epict.p.117 D

δυσφρόνη.definition: = in pl., anxieties, troubles, Hes.Th.102; in Pi.O.2.52, should be read for cf

δυσχώρητος.definition: hard to traverse: inextricable; difficult to digest, Aët.9.30

δυσώνης.definition: one who beats down the price, hard bargainer, Lync. ap. Ath.6.228c; Com.Adesp.277

δυσώπημα.definition: a means of making one ashamed, and so, a corrective, J.BJ1.25.5, cf. D.Chr.Fr.8

δυσωρέομαι.definition: keep painful watch, Il.10.183; but Apollon.Lex. read cf. Hsch., EM292.49

δύω.definition: of Places or Countries, enter, make one's way into, in Hom. the most freq. use, . . Il.22.99; Od.7.18; plunged into the clouds, of a star, Il.11.63; plunge into the lap of Ocean, 18.140; went beneath the earth, i.e. d…

δώμημα.definition: chamber, Benndorf- Niemann Reisen in Lykienp.80 No.59

δέ.definition: but: adversative and copulative Particle; answering to , Th.1.12, etc

δή.definition: prop. a temporal Particle , at this or; in Ep. sts. at the beginning of a sentence or clause, Il.15.437; 19.342; 13.122; 1.476, 13.719, al., cf. Pi.O.3.25, A.Th.214 : but usu. second , freq. with Numerals and temporal…

δηθά.definition: Ep. Adv. = for a long time, Il.10.52; ib.5.587; not long after, A.R.2.651

δηθάκι.definition: and Adv. often, Nic.Al.215, Man.3.22, Opp.C.1.27, etc

δημόθεν.definition: Adv. at the public cost; from among the people, A.R.1.7

δήποτε.definition: indef. Adv. , Ion; with interrog., what in the world? what or why now? D.4.35; . .; how many do you suppose? Id.20.21

δήπου.definition: indef. Adv. perhaps, it; as interrog. implying an affirm. answer, i.e. I presume you know, S.Tr.418; Pl.Tht.159b; surely it is not so? implying a neg. answer, as Ar.Ra.526, Pl.Men.73c

δῆτα.definition: Adv., lengthd. and more emphatic form of; in answers, mostly added to a word which echoes a statement or question, as . . Answ. aye they know, E.Med.1373; . .; Answ. yes we know her, Ar.Th.606, cf. Eq.6, al.; Answ. A.…

διά.definition: poet. , Prep. governing gen. and acc.- Rad. sense, through; never anastroph. [Prop. but Hom. uses at the beginning of a line, Il.3.357, 4.135, al.: also metri gr., freq. in Hom., for which A. uses in lyr., Ag.448, al.…

δίαντα.definition: Adv. right through, prob. in Emp.84.9

διαχείρως.definition: Adv. in the appropriate manner , Zos.Alch.p.108B

διό.definition: Conj., for wherefore, on which account, Pl.R.358d, etc.; Th.2.21, Pl.Cra.412a, al.; Id.Phdr.258e, Smp.203c; Th.1.71, 120, 8.92, etc

διότι.definition: Conj. for . . (cf; indirect, wherefore, for what reason, . . Hdt.2.24; . . Th.1.77; . . Henioch.4.7

δισσαχῇ.definition: Adv. at two points, Arist.de An.406b32

διχῆ.definition: Adv. = in two, asunder, A.Supp.544; in two ways, Id.R.445d; D.1.18

διχθά.definition: Adv., Ep. for they are parted in twain, Od.1.23; my heart is divided, Il.16.435

διχῶς.definition: Adv. doubly, in two ways, A.Ch.915 , Arist.Mu.393a24, Ascl.Tact.10.10; in two senses, Arist.Po.1457a28

δόμονδε.definition: Adv. homeward, Hom.; to his own house, Od.1.83; also Archestr.Fr.26

δράγδην.definition: Adv. in the grasp, with the hand, Plu.2.418e, Q.S.13.91
